name: RAG 101.md
text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines retrieval with language generation. A query first finds relevant passages in a knowledge base. The generator then receives the question and those passages as context. Retrieval narrows the model's evidence base; generation turns the evidence into a readable response. A grounded system should say when the retrieved evidence is insufficient.

name: Embeddings and Vector Stores.md
text: An embedding is a numeric representation of text. Similar meanings tend to be close in vector space, so vector search can retrieve passages even when the query uses different words. A vector store keeps embeddings alongside chunk IDs and metadata such as document name and page. Similarity is a ranking signal, not a probability of truth.

name: Chunking Strategies.md
text: Chunking divides a document into bounded passages before indexing. Chunks that are too large waste context and mix unrelated ideas. Chunks that are too small lose the local explanation needed to answer a question. Overlap preserves continuity across boundaries. A practical starting point is 500 to 900 tokens with 10 to 20 percent overlap, then evaluate on real questions.

name: BM25 Keyword Search.md
text: BM25 stands for Best Matching 25. It is a lexical ranking function used by search engines to score documents against a query using term frequency, inverse document frequency, document length normalization, and tunable k1 and b parameters. BM25 is strong for exact names, identifiers, numbers, and technical terms that appear in the source text.

name: Hybrid Retrieval.md
text: Hybrid retrieval combines sparse lexical search such as BM25 with dense vector retrieval. Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) can combine rankings without pretending that scores from different systems are directly comparable. Hybrid search often improves robustness: lexical retrieval catches exact terms while dense retrieval catches paraphrases.

name: Grounding and Citations.md
text: Grounding means the answer is supported by retrieved evidence. The application should pass source IDs with the context, require citations in the generated response, and validate every cited ID against the retrieved records. If evidence does not support the question, the system should say so instead of filling gaps with general knowledge.

name: RAG Evaluation.md
text: RAG evaluation separates retrieval quality from generation quality. Useful signals include recall of relevant chunks, citation validity, answer faithfulness, answer relevance, and unsupported-question behavior. Measure latency for query processing, retrieval, generation, and the total request. Do not present raw ranking scores as calibrated probabilities.

name: Latency Optimization.md
text: Latency comes from ingestion, query embedding, retrieval, context assembly, and generation. Keep chunk context bounded, cache stable embeddings, stream generation when the product needs it, and measure each stage separately. A faster answer is not automatically better if it omits the evidence needed for grounding.

name: Knowledge Base Updates.md
text: When a source changes, remove or replace its old chunks and vectors before adding the new version. Stable document and chunk identifiers make deletion auditable. Reindexing should expose its state and any extraction errors. Duplicate ingestion should be detected by source identity or content hash.
